method: Independent manual sequential inspection of all108 final runtime cells, all nine seams with last3/first3 native-size neighbor sheets, native return01 first6/return02 last6 strips, and native turn-exit/next-stage strips. seams.observation: The closed-eye smiling entry opens into a normal face while crossed ankles reset to parallel feet. Head size and crown height remain close. The blink is natural, but the one-cell foot reset remains visible.
Both frontal clasped-hand neutral cells agree in stance, head tilt and floor. Small changes in hair ends, cape edge, skirt flare and facial linework remain between drawn families.
Same frontal hands-together pose and parallel shoes continue into the next stage. Crown and face positions stay close; hair/eye rendering changes slightly without a large scale step.
The front standing pose and clasped hands match into the turn entrance. Segment04 then extends hands in genuine successive drawn poses. Hair curls and cape/hem outlines change a little at the cut.

The turn exits as a screen-right profile and the next frame remains a screen-right profile, so there is no cafe-like yaw back-step. However, outstretched hands fold quickly from ahead of the body to close together near the chin in one cell; the bent lifted-foot stance also changes slightly. A small but visible arm/posture step remains.

The closed-eye smile, raised screen-left arm, slight head tilt and same bent/lifted leg agree across the cut. The continuation keeps comparable face/body size and stance. Hair/cape outline and the exact raised fingers vary a little, without a large hand/foot relocation.

In the actual final pixels the lifted/crossed shoe sits toward screen-left and the planted shoe toward screen-right on both sides of the boundary. Return01 preserves this same lifted leg, gradually lowering it through several real poses until both feet are grounded; it does not exchange the lifted and planted legs. Raised arm lowers progressively. Minor hand/face/cape linework changes remain.

Return01 ends with both feet parallel and the screen-left arm approximately horizontal. Return02 keeps those grounded feet, lifts/straightens the arm slightly at its first frame, then lowers it toward neutral. The head straightens a little and the cape opens enough to change the blouse/hair layering. No major size or foot-phase pop.

Both bookends are front standing with arms relaxed and parallel grounded shoes, and maintain close head/body height. Hair curls, face shading and foot spacing vary a little between independent neutral drawings. The loop has no conspicuous return-to-entry size collapse or crown jump; it is not a pixel-identical bookend.

return_leg_phase: Lifted shoe appears toward screen-left and planted shoe toward screen-right in final Segment06/11 and Return01/00. Return01 gradually returns that same lifted leg to the floor; actual poses have been checked, not merely source independence.
remaining_minor: Segment04/11→segment05/00 quick outstretched-to-clasped arm change while maintaining the same right-facing profile.
Across independent drawn families, modest hair/cape/hem/face rendering differences; loop neutral slightly different foot spacing/shading.
overall: The final travel108 sequence maintains Cecilia identity, bare mint hair and the raspberry travel cape/white blouse/blue tie/navy skirt outfit. No blank cell, clipping, conspicuous scale collapse or lifted/planted-leg exchange is seen. The corrected return family visibly lowers the same leg and arm into a matching-height neutral. Usable for integration with the listed small stance/arm and illustration differences; not claimed perfectly seamless.
